about: Banned expressions and constructions in the ordinary prose (doc/authoring/plain-prose.md). Each entry is earned by a sentence met in play or in the tables, kept in `evidence`, which the entry must match; each fails test/small/prose-lint wherever it is narrated in `scope`. Keep the list small: a word that is bad in one sentence and useful in others belongs in watchlist.json. An authored adventure's prose, and a going-on's, is its author's, and is not in scope. `owned`: files another agent is editing, whose findings are listed by scripts/prose-lint.ts and not failed.

banned.why: a decorative noun phrase where the event (the meal spilled) is not said
banned.evidence: With the wagoner roaring at the wheel, the cart comes up out of the ditch in a slither of meal. (data/origins/prologue.kyrt; the owner, 17 November night: 'the imagery is strained, the physical event is obscured, and the sentence sounds unpleasant')

banned.why: the narrator judging what someone is like instead of saying what they do (narratology.md's banned table, 7 November)
banned.evidence: Aldous Fenn looks you over with the air of a man sizing up timber. (data/generation/town/outskirts-deep.kyrt: the reeve's greeting, met in every a1 walk of the prose census, 17 November)

banned.why: drollery: an animal or a thing given a second thought (narratology.md's banned table, 7 November)
banned.evidence: Night comes on while you are still on the {way}. An owl keeps pace with you for a while, and then thinks better of it. (data/voice/journey.json, journey-dark.2)

banned.why: a wry tag that explains a plain act
banned.evidence: {Actor} barks twice, for form's sake, then comes to see who you are. (data/voice/greet.json, greet.dog.3: the owner's example of filler, 17 November)

banned.why: metacommentary: the narrator explaining the joke (narratology.md, 7 November)
banned.evidence: {Name} is leaning on a gate, looking at a field as though it owed them money. (data/generation/scenes/occupations.json before 14 November)
